parsed.notes: Uninventoried Lens A issues observed: content Background names Kayla Chisholm, but the opinion text names Brittany Chisholm; content Application says a single uncorroborated address, while the opinion says the residence conclusion rested on two CJLEADS entries and Brinkley's public Facebook; the Payton quote in Rule changes the original terminal period to a comma.

reasons: Lake identity identifies United States v. Kendrick Brinkley, decided 2020-11-13, docket 18-4455, in the Fourth Circuit.
Lake citation display and official citation are 980 F.3d 377; content renders 980 F.3d 377 (4th Cir. 2020).
residual_risks: Frontmatter citation field alone says 980 F.3d 377 (2020), but the separate court field supplies 4th Cir. 2020 and the rendered citation is complete.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If the citation field is intended to be self-contained, use 980 F.3d 377 (4th Cir. 2020).

reasons: The opinion is centrally about officers entering a private home to execute an arrest warrant without consent or a search warrant.
The majority resolves Payton's home-entry standard and reverses denial of suppression for failure to satisfy the residence and presence prongs.
residual_risks: Role labels are editorial, but the disclosed opinion text supports treating this as a key Arrest in the Home case.

reasons: The opinion holds that Payton's reasonable-belief standard requires probable cause in the Fourth Circuit.
The opinion states police needed probable cause that Brinkley resided at the Stoney Trace apartment and would be present when they entered.
The opinion concludes the entry was unlawful and reverses the denial of Brinkley's suppression motion, vacating the challenged convictions.
residual_risks: The holding is a compressed paraphrase; the factual record included CJLEADS, Facebook, and doorstep observations, not literally no evidence beyond an arrest warrant.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: To avoid overcompression, describe the defect as sparse, conflicting residence evidence plus generic signs of life and nervousness not particularized to Brinkley.
